description: The bar chart illustrates the Mean Average Precision at 10 (MAP@10) values for two different sampling strategies—Uniform Sampling Strategy and a second strategy represented by purple bars—across varying values of $ m $, which ranges from 6 to 10 on the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled MAP@10, is scaled from 23.0 to 27.0 in increments of 0.5, with gridlines at each 0.5 unit. The purple bars, corresponding to the second strategy, are consistently taller than the yellow bars, indicating higher MAP@10 performance across all $ m $ values. For the purple bars, the MAP@10 values increase from approximately 25.9 at $ m = 6 $ to a peak of about 26.7 at $ m = 7 $, then decrease slightly to around 26.3 at $ m = 8 $, rise again to roughly 26.5 at $ m = 9 $, and finally settle at approximately 26.4 at $ m = 10 $. In contrast, the yellow bars, representing the Uniform Sampling Strategy, show a more variable trend: starting at about 24.4 at $ m = 6 $, they increase to a peak of approximately 25.6 at $ m = 8 $, then decrease to around 25.3 at $ m = 9 $, and end at about 24.4 at $ m = 10 $. The legend in the top right corner identifies the purple bars as belonging to the second strategy and the yellow bars to the Uniform Sampling Strategy.
